title: Priority surge gates and context-aware admission for graceful degradation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a production-safe, tenant-aware load shedding mechanism that combines priority-based surge gates, context-aware admission checks, and configurable graceful degradation modes. The goal is to protect cluster SLOs (p50/p95 latency, error rate) during regional overload and multi-region failover while preserving best-effort experience for high-value tenants and critical routes. This work standardizes runtime primitives, control-plane config, and observability so operators can reason about and tune shedding behavior without code changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New priority surge gate accepts requests for three priority bands (critical, standard, best-effort) and enforces admission tokens per band
2) Runtime exposes a configurable admission policy DSL (max-inflight, token-burst, prefault allowance) per route/model and per-tenant
3) Graceful degradation actions implemented: partial-response truncation, model-fallback (large->small), compress-response flag, and early-ack (deferred completion with job id)
4) During synthetic overload tests, critical band maintains p95 latency < SLO target and error rate increase < 1% while best-effort accepts < 5% throughput of normal baseline
5) Console dashboard shows per-band throughput, rejection rate, token consumption, and per-tenant fairness score
6) Feature toggles and canary rollout path exist in runtime-2.0 release with automated rollback on regression alerts
implementation_notes: Core runtime change: add PriorityGate module to serving path that checks per-route admission policy before enqueueing into KV-batched executor
Admission tokens are decoupled from tenant quotas: tokens are short-lived credits that prevent burst storms from starving critical work
Token allocation strategy: proportional-share by committed capacity with an emergency reserve for 'critical' band (configurable)
Graceful degradation modes should be pluggable: implement ResponseTrimmer, ModelFallbackManager, and CompressedWireAdapter interfaces
Integrate with circuit breaker: if a downstream model variant crosses error threshold, update admission policy to favor fallback variants automatically
Avoid head-of-line blocking: admission check must be O(1) and non-blocking; token check uses in-memory counters with eventual persistence to metering store for accounting
Edge case: multi-region failover must apply neighbor-region limits to prevent cascading overload — use geofencing config with per-region token pools
test_plan: Unit tests for token allocator, fairness calculator, and Policy DSL parsing
Integration tests: simulate 100k RPS with mixed priority distribution and assert SLOs for critical band
Chaos test: bring down model variant in region A and verify failover and admission adjustments in region B
Load replay: run 7-day production traffic replay and validate request trimming doesn't introduce unacceptable regressions in quality metrics
Customer-facing e2e: QA with internal tenant workloads for billing and audit correctness
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary in prod-small (10% traffic) with synthetic spike generator
Phase 1: opt-in customers via feature flag for dedicated capacity accounts
Phase 2: progressive rollout to 50% of serving fleet with automated SLO guardrails (auto rollback on >2% p95 regression)
Phase 3: full rollout and deprecation of legacy soft-shedder code path
Operator runbook: steps to change band weights, disable fallback, and emergency drain instructions
monitoring: Key metrics: band_throughput, band_reject_rate, token_pool_utilization, fallback_ratio, trimmed_tokens_saved
Alerts: p95_critical_latency > SLO for 5m, reject_rate_critical > 0.1% sustained, fairness_score_drop > 20%
Tracing: attach admission_reason tag to traces to correlate user-visible errors with shedding decisions
open_questions: Q1: Default band mapping for new routes — should we infer from route SLA or require explicit mapping?
Q2: How to bill for partially-trimmed responses? (token billing vs successful-response billing vs hybrid)
Q3: Emergency reserve sizing policy for multi-tenant Dedicated pools — percentage or absolute tokens?
Q4: Backwards compatibility with client SDKs that rely on exact response shapes when truncation occurs
